triage.verifier_justification: The diff changes the Brazil IEEPA term's gate in two derived rules (ieepa_component_rate and ieepa_component_rate_with_declared_exceptions) from the witness's per-line exemplar flag `entry_is_line_b` to the source concept `entry_is_section_232_aluminum`, so encoded meaning and the module's input surface change, not just provenance. Both the pre and post files carry the same unchanged exception proof atom — "The additional duties imposed by heading 9903.01.77 shall not apply to products of aluminum provided for in heading 9903.85.02." (us/statute/hts/chapter-99/page-219) — and I confirmed that text in the pinned release us-rulespec-2026-08-08-obbb-alien-snap (2026-08-01-usitc-hts-2026-rev3-notes.jsonl, note 2(x)(vii) at chapter-99/page-220), so the pre-fix condition was a harness artifact with no basis in the cited note: nothing in the source refers to any "line b". That is untraceable_branch ("re-grounds" a condition), not unrepresented_clause (nothing is added) and not amount/boundary/date; the competing reading is wrong_entity_or_scope, since the effect is an exclusion scoped to one exemplar line instead of the §232 aluminum population. The steel half of the diff (9903.81.87/.88 → 9903.82.02, `source:` string plus proof-atom citation paths) is provenance-only — rate '0.50' and excerpt text are identical — so it is mechanical on its own and does not carry the verdict.

triage.verifier_notes:
Refutation attempts that failed: (1) "generated composition, not an encoded module" — the file is `format: rulespec/v1`, `module.kind: composition`, with rules, formulas, versions and proof atoms; its encoded meaning changed, so not_a_rule_module/mechanical do not apply. (2) "enhancement, not defect" — the pre file's own summary already states "Membership-semantic China-301 list123/list4A, section-232 aluminum/steel, section-201 CSPV, section-122 exemption, and section-232-covered identifiers are caller inputs supplied by entry preparation" and that only "Beer/section-338 keeps entry_is_line_d", while the Brazil formula still used entry_is_line_b — an internal inconsistency showing a leftover exemplar artifact in a module that claims chapter scale, not new coverage.

Caveats a reviewer should weigh (why I did not go above ~0.72): (a) For this particular module — chapter 74, copper — the change is numerically inert: no chapter-74 line can be `entry_is_line_b` (the witness exemplar is 7601.10.30.00, aluminum) nor `entry_is_section_232_aluminum`, so both gates evaluate the same for real ch74 entries. The candidate reason's harm sentence ("Brazilian aluminum entries ... received a duty") is true of the generated family (identical hunks in all 100 module files in this commit; the real fix is in tools/generate_schedule_compositions.py), not of ch74 in isolation. (b) The chapter-relevant exclusion for copper — note 2(x)(xi), "The additional duties imposed by heading 9903.01.77 shall not apply to semi-finished copper and intensive copper derivative products provided for in heading 9903.78.01" — is encoded neither before nor after, as are (v)/(vi) steel and (viii) derivative aluminum; that residual gap is a separate unrepresented_clause, untouched by this commit. (c) `entry_is_reciprocal_metals_excluded` still has `formula: entry_is_line_b` post-fix (post line 1924) under a 9903.01.33 atom reading "articles of aluminum; derivative articles of aluminum" — same defect class, left in place.

Source checks run (read-only): resolve_provision.py on us/statute/hts/chapter-99/page-219 at rulespec commit 198bee703e resolved to the rev3 notes file where page numbering differs from the module's "Rev. 15 vintage"; I located the note text by scanning that single jsonl. In the same release's current HTS provisions file, 9903.82.02 exists ("articles of aluminum, of steel or of copper and derivative aluminum or steel articles ... U.S. note 16 ... + 50%") while 9903.81.87/.88 do not, corroborating the commit report's "stale locator" claim for the steel citation. Also visible at this commit: section_232_steel_component_rate carries a doubled `metadata: proof: proof: atoms:` wrapper, which the PR's later maintainer comment says was unwrapped in a follow-up ("steel atoms unwrapped to canonical `metadata.proof.atoms`").
